summary.text: A 67-year-old man with a 15-year history of insulin-treated type 2 diabetes with suboptimal control, essential hypertension, chronic pancreatitis and a 45-pack-year smoking history presented to the emergency department with loss of consciousness and a blood glucose of 2.6 mmol/L, and regained consciousness after the hypoglycemia was corrected. An obvious right facial nerve palsy had lasted three weeks, and he was known to ENT with ear disease and a recent diabetic ketoacidosis admission.

He had persistent right ear pain, minimal discharge and reduced hearing, previously treated with oral co-amoxiclav and ear spray. Examination and a full cranial nerve examination found multiple cranial nerve abnormalities, and the ear swab grew ciprofloxacin-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. CRP and white cell count were raised, CT showed destruction of the right petrous apex and skull base, and MRI showed extensive right necrotizing otitis externa with skull base osteomyelitis and granulation tissue at the osseocartilaginous junction; Doppler ultrasound excluded thrombosis.

The skull base multidisciplinary team ruled out a neoplastic process and confirmed necrotizing otitis externa with skull base osteomyelitis, likely complex and Carney Stage 3b, with conservative management advised. Intravenous co-amoxiclav was escalated to tazocin and then ceftazidime for six weeks, insulin was titrated for glycemic control, and a right tarsorrhaphy treated exposure keratitis.

Before discharge, ear pain, discharge and the right facial palsy had improved. Inflammatory markers were reported back to normal. At follow-up 10 days after discharge, both tympanic membranes were intact without infection or granulation, and the cranial nerve palsy had resolved, although hearing loss persisted.
